cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: Each turn takes up the prior term: T5 tallying, T6 test, T8 gift of information, T9 pause.
cells.limitation: Realist never answers T9's objection that the pause is ambiguous.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces disclosure-versus-test, absent from openings; T7 and T10 build on it.
cells.limitation: T9's scorekeeping point about the pause is not developed by any later turn.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2 and T5 weigh mutuality against accepting a warm, lopsided friendship.
cells.limitation: The less-invested possibility from Section A is never examined head-on in any turn.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T4 accepts T3's no-verdict point; T10 accepts light and curious from T6.
cells.limitation: Realist's view is not reshaped by others; it stays fixed from T2 to T8.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T10 narrows the dispute to timing: speak then observe versus observe then speak.
cells.limitation: Section D's main insight stays abstract: one fact is clear, the other a guess.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 states both prior stories fairly: neglect versus temperament.
cells.limitation: T5 attacks talk as a disguised test, a version T1 and T4 never proposed.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T8 targets T7's assumption the friend lacks information: then the gift lands as pressure.
cells.limitation: T10 does not answer T8's they-know-already objection; it restates a timing preference.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T6's impact-not-intent framing fits Difficult Conversations accurately.
cells.limitation: T1's voice is cheaper than leaving sits oddly with Hirschman's stress on voice's costs (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T3 says Why is a guess; T8 marks I go further than Montaigne here.
cells.limitation: T1 asserts resentment grows quietly as a general fact without qualification.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T4 Fair, T5 I grant that, T7 sharpens my view: concessions with named causes.
cells.limitation: Realist never concedes or answers T9's critique of the pause.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A separates changing the friendship from wanting it to feel more mutual.
cells.limitation: The likely concern of feeling less valued is only named obliquely in Section D.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T2 uses the meetings are lovely; T3 uses when texts stop, plans stop.
cells.limitation: Texting as the channel and the user's planning role are not used beyond T8.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E keys options to whether the imbalance weighs on the user.
cells.limitation: T5's preference to leave warm ties unexamined is the speaker's value, not separated from the user's.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T1 names the stakes: carrying effort until tired or fading out.
cells.limitation: How much this friend matters and the pattern's length are never weighed or asked.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches: burden or scorekeeping favours talking; no weight favours doing nothing.
cells.limitation: The friend's possible reasons in Section A get no per-reason branch.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section D asks: bothered by how it feels, or by what it says about the friend?
cells.limitation: Motives surface only in Sections A and D, not within the debate turns.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T2 challenges treating the imbalance as a flaw; T3 splits fact from story.
cells.limitation: The user's own role, perhaps planning before the friend can, is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D asks whether a warm but lopsided friendship is a problem at all.
cells.limitation: Reciprocity versus warmth as competing values is implied, never put to the user directly.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T4 and T9 name silent tallying and private scorekeeping without pathologising.
cells.limitation: Fear of hearing the friend cares less, or of seeming needy, is never named.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T6 offers a disclosure script the user can adapt or reject.
cells.limitation: Section D's question offers no implication for either answer.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lays out talking, doing nothing, pausing, or a casual remark.
cells.limitation: T1's fading-out option is dropped from Section E's options.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T8 costs talking as pressure; T9 costs pausing as ambiguity and scorekeeping.
cells.limitation: Doing nothing's cost, continued one-sided effort, is absent from Section E.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: noticing yourself keeping score favours a light conversation.
cells.limitation: Which friend responses favour which option is left open; T8's few weeks is ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section A flags the friend's reason and the user's want as the decisive unknowns.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not separated from the two consequential ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: Section E offers a casual remark script, a light, low-cost step.
cells.limitation: T8's few-week pause length is not derived from the user's facts.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T3 plain: one fact, when texts stop, plans stop.
cells.limitation: T1 uses Hirschman's voice and leaving as terms without explaining them.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T10 names the Realist explicitly when stating the remaining dispute.
cells.limitation: T2's You are treating the imbalance blurs whether the user or Voice Advocate is meant.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within 25 to 65 words; Sections D and E stay brief.
cells.limitation: none

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Positions differ clearly; T7 and T10 mark explicit shifts in the Voice Advocate.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one plain register and near-equal turn lengths, T1 to T10.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: T10's recap of the timing dispute serves the close rather than repeating.
cells.limitation: Section D repeats Section A's fact-versus-guess framing.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T1 versus T5: quiet drain against turning a friend into a defendant.
cells.limitation: The risk of losing the friendship stays muted after T1.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 shifts complaint to gift of information, traced to T6's disclosure.
cells.limitation: Shifts are narrowings, not surprises; no mind reverses on its central claim.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T5's Realist is wry: That turns a friend into a defendant.
cells.limitation: Montaigne's mind lacks Montaigne's digressive voice; expression is flat across T1 to T10.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3 turn a puzzle into an accusation; T4 a polite way of never speaking.
cells.limitation: No concrete scene or example of the friendship enlivens any turn.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T8's pause proposal briefly raises suspense before T9 undercuts it.
cells.limitation: Steady, even rhythm from T1 to T10; intensity barely varies.

strengths: T6's disclosure-versus-test distinction reshapes the Voice Advocate in T7 and T10.
Section E maps observable conditions (burden, scorekeeping) to talking or doing nothing.
Tight continuity: T4 to T9 each pick up the previous turn's specific term.
weaknesses: No mind names the fear of learning the friend cares less, T1 to T10.
T1 attributes voice is cheaper than leaving to Hirschman, which is suspect.
All three minds share one plain register; the Realist does not sound like Montaigne.

symptoms.observed: Names scorekeeping but never the fear of what the friend's answer could reveal.
symptoms.evidence: you would have learned nothing while privately keeping score

symptoms.observed: The less-invested reading of the friend's silence is never argued in any turn.
symptoms.evidence: Or they know perfectly well and are content to be invited.

symptoms.observed: Attributes a cost claim to Hirschman that his framing of voice does not obviously support.
Even turn lengths and one calm register; no build or release of intensity.
symptoms.evidence: Some people simply are not initiators, yet give full attention once together.

symptoms.observed: Never weighs how much this friend matters or how long the pattern has run.
symptoms.evidence: That may be the whole of what this friend offers

findings.description: Hirschman generally presents voice as costlier than exit; attributing voice is cheaper than leaving to him may misstate his view.
Some ties are better left unexamined is offered under Montaigne's Essays; fit with his writing on friendship could not be assessed.
A few weeks of pausing is proposed with no derivation from the user's facts.

rubric_fit_notes: The Hirschman concern rests on my memory of his argument, not on attached evidence, so it is reported as suspected only.
question_type_note: Read as a decision about whether and how to raise the initiating imbalance, with every cell applied as written.
